I once helped this couple bring their belongings on the bus and across the city. I think they were homeless, not sure. They were downtown and weren't very good with directions. I was heading to the same area of the city they were, so I offered to tag along and help. On the way they were picking up cigarette butts off the ground to break apart and smoke later. This is so unhygienic :( I've never smoked cigarettes and never will. Smokers are jokers.

Anyway, near where they were going, we stopped by at a grocery store so they could get a couple things. They thanked me for my help and we parted ways. I went to the front of the store and picked up their brand of smokes, walked over to them and said "hey you dropped this". Handed it over, walked away. They didn't say anything. I didn't want them to say anything. It just felt so damn good to do that for them, even though it was $10 or whatever, it made me feel like a million bucks. Never seen/heard from them again, hope they're alright.

I think the one "random act of kindness" I've ever done that's ever truly affected someone was back when I worked at a grocery store as a teenager. A woman came through the checkout with her child, she was really only buying the essentials, food and what not. I rang her up and, just as you may have expected, her card didn't work. Now, she was only buying something like $30 of food so I decided to cover her purchase. I mean, I as ~16 years old really only spent my money on video games and pot, so $30 would have been better spent on feeding a family. It took a lot of convincing to get her to take my money but I told her she can take it and not worrying about paying me back. She thanked me a lot. I saw her again almost 2 months later and she came over and thanked me again and told me that she never forgot the day I helped her.

The feeling that you actually made an impact on someones day is an amazing feeling and that sticks with you for the rest of the day.
